memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph had his chariot made ready and went to Goshen to meet his father Israel. As soon as Joseph appeared before him, he threw his arms around his father and wept for a long time." — Gen 46:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The most powerful man in Egypt after Pharaoh gets into his chariot and drives out to a shepherds' district to meet an old man. And when he sees his father, all the authority falls away. He throws his arms around him and weeps — the text says, for a long time.

Twenty-two years of separation end in that embrace. Everything Joseph achieved in Egypt, all the honour and the titles, and this is the moment he had actually been waiting for.

There is a lesson buried in that chariot ride. Joseph did not summon his father to the palace; he went to Goshen himself. Love goes to people. It does not wait for them to arrive at the appropriate address.

That is what God has done. He did not require us to climb to Him. The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us (Jn 1:14). Christ came down into our Goshen — into the dust and the poverty and the mess — because that is what love does.

And there is a reunion still ahead for the people of God, when every separation is finally over and there is no more parting (1 Thess 4:17). If Joseph wept for a long time on that road, imagine that day.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who do you need to go to rather than waiting for them to come to you?
2. What does it mean to you that Christ came down to where you were?
3. What reunion are you longing for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You came down to where I was rather than waiting for me to climb to You. Give me a love like that for others, and hold my hope for the day when all partings end. Amen.
